title: Session pro-rated ingress/egress billing proxy experiment
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Run a controlled field experiment that charges for sessions using a pro-rated approach to ingress (input) and egress (output) tokens to evaluate whether per-session minimums, pro-rating across short sessions, and asymmetric IO rates improve unit economics without materially harming latency-sensitive streaming adoption. This ticket covers experiment design, telemetry, enterprise contract/SQ alignment, and the initial two-week pilot on a small PLG segment.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented metering for per-request direction (ingress v. egress) at session granularity
Experiment variants implemented behind feature flag and reversible in 24h
Legal/SQ sign-off on wording for enterprise T&Cs and sample invoice line items
Dashboard visualizing revenue delta, active sessions, average tokens/session, and churn by cohort
Rollback plan documented and tested for customer-facing invoice errors
metrics: Net revenue delta (USD) vs. baseline by cohort
Change in average tokens per session (input/output)
Churn signal: customers with >10% invoice change flagged
Billing disputes and SQ-related legal requests count
proposed_variants: Control: current per-direction per-token billing with existing minimums
Variant A: per-session pro-rate — prorate minimum across sessions within 24h window
Variant B: asymmetric directional rates — ingress charged at 0.6x of egress for streaming sessions
Variant C: session floor smoothing — small sessions get rounded up but aggregated by session-group over billing period
rollout_plan: Week 0: infra + metering changes merged to canary; internal billing sandbox validation
Week 1: small PLG cohort (5% new signups) for 14-day pilot; finance watches disputes daily
Week 2: expand to 20% PLG and 10% existing non-enterprise customers if no regressions
Week 3: enterprise pilot outreach for 3 willing customers; get SQ/legal feedback and invoice sample approvals
Abort criteria: >2% uplift in churn in pilot cohort, >0.5% of bills disputed, or regressed revenue >3% after 7 days
notes: Motivation: customers complain about short-lived streaming sessions where minimums dominate cost — we hypothesize pro-rating reduces friction and encourages more streaming usage while preserving revenue for long-running sessions.

Trade-offs: pro-rating reduces per-bill noise for small users but may lower ARPU for some heavy-output use-cases; asymmetric rates could encourage longer context send vs generated tokens shifting model load.
Implementation details: require tagging of session start/stop in request pipeline, accumulation table per-session id for billing window, and safe-export to reconciliation ledger in billing service.

SQ/contract alignment: engage Legal + Sales Ops to update sample contract language for enterprise customers who request per-session invoicing; prepare FAQ for customer support and SSO/SAML teams regarding audit trails.
